title: Lincoln's history as a segregated school in a prejudiced town
summary: Lincoln was founded by Civil War veterans, had 300 students, was coed and accredited. Jefferson City was as prejudiced as Webster Groves.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: ... AND A very prejudiced town. I mean it's not more prejudiced than Webster Groves because you had the same situation that happened and dastardly. Total resentment about them, you know.
But, Lincoln University, was that segregated?

Yes, definitely. Some fellows from the Civil War decided to establish a school there and they did. By what means, I mean getting the state to back them, I don't know. They came from the Civil War and they decided to establish a school. Don't ask for the year because I wan give you ... wouldn't
Well, how big a school would it be?
For a high school, that's a fair size.
No, a college, too. Accredited. High school and college.
And, was it all boys or wait it ... was
Oh, no, it was integrated. I mean coed. Yes and we had prime (?) teachers. And we were a accredited school north centrally ...
Well, really since Webster Groves was so far away, you were very lucky you went there.

Stan, you don't know. You really don't know. As the years pass by, I was very fortunate I could go there. I think it's one of the finest things that ever happened to me. I mentioned the tremendous people there. I think ... musical. I mean everything that happens is musical. Let me tell you about this incident, if I may.
